average_male_professional.name: Basic Male Health Stack
average_male_professional.description: For the average Indian professional male, 25-45, sedentary to moderately active. Addresses the most common deficiencies in Indian men.

supplements.name: Vitamin B12
supplements.why: 47-75% of Indian adults are deficient, especially vegetarians

supplements.name: Omega-3
supplements.dosage: 1000 mg fish oil (or 1 tbsp ground flaxseeds)
supplements.why: Indian diets have poor omega-6:omega-3 ratio (15-20:1 vs ideal 2-4:1)

supplements.name: Vitamin D3 + K2
supplements.why: 70-100% of Indians are Vitamin D deficient

supplements.name: Magnesium Glycinate
supplements.when: Evening with dinner or before bed
supplements.why: 50-80% of Indians don't meet magnesium RDA; supports sleep and muscle recovery

average_female_professional.name: Basic Female Health Stack
average_female_professional.description: For the average Indian professional female, 25-45. Addresses higher iron needs, bone health, and common deficiencies.

supplements.name: Vitamin B12
supplements.why: Critical for vegetarian women; deficiency causes anemia and nerve issues

supplements.name: Iron (ferrous bisglycinate) + Vitamin C
supplements.why: ~50% of Indian women are anemic. ONLY if blood test confirms deficiency or heavy menstruation.

supplements.name: Vitamin D3 + K2
supplements.why: Women especially affected by Vitamin D deficiency in India

supplements.name: Omega-3
supplements.dosage: 1000 mg fish oil or algae-based EPA/DHA
supplements.why: Heart health, anti-inflammation, mood support

supplements.name: Magnesium Glycinate
supplements.why: Helps with PMS symptoms, sleep, anxiety, and bone health

supplements.name: Calcium Citrate
supplements.why: If dairy intake is low; critical for bone density

male_gym_goer.name: Active Male / Gym-Goer Stack
male_gym_goer.description: For active/gym-going Indian males. Includes base stack plus performance supplements. Supports muscle building, recovery, and higher activity demands.

supplements.name: Vitamin B12
supplements.why: Base deficiency coverage

supplements.name: Vitamin D3 + K2
supplements.why: Supports testosterone, bone health, and immune function

supplements.name: Omega-3
supplements.why: Anti-inflammatory support for recovery

supplements.name: Whey/Plant Protein
supplements.why: Most Indians don't meet protein targets; critical for muscle building

supplements.name: Creatine Monohydrate
supplements.when: Any time (consistency matters more than timing)
supplements.why: Most researched supplement in sports nutrition; safe, effective for strength and muscle

supplements.name: Zinc
supplements.why: Lost in sweat; supports testosterone and recovery

supplements.name: Magnesium Glycinate
supplements.why: Lost in sweat; supports sleep, recovery, reduces cramps

female_active.name: Active Female Stack
female_active.description: For active Indian women who exercise regularly. Addresses higher nutrient demands from exercise and common female-specific deficiencies.

supplements.name: Vitamin B12
supplements.why: Base coverage

supplements.name: Vitamin D3 + K2
supplements.why: Bone health, immune function, muscle recovery

supplements.name: Iron (if deficient)
supplements.dosage: 15-30 mg ferrous bisglycinate + 200 mg Vitamin C
supplements.why: Higher iron needs from menstruation + exercise. Blood test first.

supplements.name: Whey/Plant Protein
supplements.why: Women often under-consume protein; 1.4-1.8 g/kg recommended for active women

supplements.name: Omega-3
supplements.why: Anti-inflammatory, joint support, mood

supplements.name: Calcium Citrate
supplements.why: Bone density protection, especially important for active women

supplements.name: Magnesium Glycinate
supplements.why: Sleep, recovery, PMS support, cramp prevention

optional_add_ons.name: Creatine Monohydrate
optional_add_ons.condition: Equally beneficial for women; no virilizing effects

stress_sleep_stack.name: Stress & Sleep Recovery Stack
stress_sleep_stack.description: Targeted stack for Indian professionals dealing with chronic stress, anxiety, and poor sleep quality.

supplements.name: Ashwagandha KSM-66
supplements.dosage: 600 mg/day (300 mg morning + 300 mg before bed)
supplements.when: Morning with breakfast and before bed
supplements.why: Reduces cortisol by 27.9%, improves sleep quality, reduces anxiety

supplements.name: Magnesium Glycinate
supplements.why: Calms nervous system, improves sleep quality, reduces anxiety and muscle tension

supplements.name: L-Theanine
supplements.when: Before bed (or 100 mg with morning tea for calm focus)
supplements.why: Promotes relaxation without sedation, improves sleep quality

supplements.name: Omega-3
supplements.why: EPA has anti-depressive and anti-inflammatory effects

supplements.name: Vitamin D3
supplements.why: Deficiency linked to depression and poor mood

supplements.name: Vitamin B12
supplements.why: Deficiency contributes to fatigue and mood disturbance

optional_add_ons.name: Melatonin
optional_add_ons.condition: For sleep onset difficulty (short-term use preferred)

optional_add_ons.name: Brahmi (Bacopa monnieri)
optional_add_ons.condition: If experiencing brain fog alongside stress

skin_hair_stack.name: Skin & Hair Health Stack
skin_hair_stack.description: Targeted stack for skin and hair health concerns, common among Indian professionals due to stress, pollution, and nutritional gaps.

supplements.name: Vitamin D3
supplements.why: Deficiency linked to hair loss and poor skin health; 70-100% Indians are deficient

supplements.name: Vitamin C
supplements.why: Collagen synthesis, antioxidant, protects skin from UV and pollution damage

supplements.name: Vitamin E
supplements.why: Skin antioxidant protection, works synergistically with Vitamin C

supplements.name: Zinc
supplements.why: Critical for hair follicle health, wound healing, acne reduction

supplements.name: Omega-3
supplements.why: Anti-inflammatory; supports skin hydration and reduces acne

supplements.name: Biotin (Vitamin B7)
supplements.why: Supports keratin production for hair and nails. Note: can interfere with some lab tests - inform your doctor.

supplements.name: Iron (if deficient)
supplements.when: Morning on empty stomach with Vitamin C
supplements.why: Iron deficiency is the most common nutritional cause of hair loss in Indian women. Blood test required.

lifestyle_additions: Scalp massage 4 min/day (Koyama et al., 2016: increased hair thickness)
Adequate protein intake (hair is made of keratin, a protein)
Stress management (cortisol is the #1 modifiable factor for hair loss)
Adequate hydration (2-3 liters/day in Indian climate)
